references.text: Ezekiel quotes directly from Leviticus 18:5 and confirms that the one who keeps God's statutes and laws shall live by them.
Nehemiah refers to God's commands and laws as those by which a person shall live, a direct allusion to this verse.
Moses exhorts the people to keep the statutes and laws so that they may live and enter the land.
The promise of life by walking in the Lord's ways and keeping His commandments.
Moses sets before the people the choice between life and death, blessing and curse, tied to obedience to God's commands.
Paul quotes Leviticus 18:5 to describe the righteousness that comes from the law, in contrast to the righteousness of faith.
Paul quotes this verse to show that the law is not based on faith but on works.
Jesus says to the expert in the law, 'Do this and you will live' – an allusion to the promise in Leviticus 18:5.
The promise of security in the land by keeping God's statutes and laws.
Ezekiel describes Israel's rebellion against God's laws by which a person should live.
Repeated reference to God's statutes that give life to those who keep them.
